title: World's Tallest Wooden Pagoda: 970 Years Old, Too Fragile to Climb | China Travel Expert
description:
The Pagoda of Fogong Temple in Shanxi — better known as the Yingxian Wooden Pagoda — is the tallest wooden pagoda on Earth. Guinness World Records certified it in 2016 at about 67 metres. It was built in 1056, which makes it nearly 970 years old, and it was raised almost entirely with interlocking timber joints — almost no nails.

Five storeys show on the outside, nine levels hide within. But you can't climb it anymore: ageing timber and leaning columns made the upper floors unsafe, so they've been closed to visitors since 2011. Today you stand at the base and look up.

🧭 Expert Tip: Pair it with the Hanging Temple and the Yungang Grottoes near Datong — the three sit close together and make one unforgettable Shanxi loop.

世界最高木塔——应县木塔（佛宫寺释迦塔），1056 年建，约 67 米，几乎不用一根钉子；因年久倾斜，2011 年起上层停止对外开放。
